ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based PEP screening at shareholder, UBO, and manager level under the Law of 12 November 2004; cross-verification against UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List (for USD-denominated Stripe and Shopify Payments rails), Luxembourg Ministry of Finance national designations, and INTERPOL notices; Enhanced Due Diligence required for any PEP, high-risk third-country, or adverse-media exposure before KYC acceptance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) digital portal - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); filing access via https://www.lbr.lu and Guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin-script characters; statutory documents and registered corporate objects must be drafted in French; foreign-language names require a French, German, or Luxembourgish transliteration where phonetically necessary; the name must not breach public policy or mislead as to the company's actual activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within three months of refusal notification, the applicant may file a formal administrative appeal with the Tribunal administratif under the consolidated Law of 1 December 1978 on administrative procedure; alternatively, a modified name may be resubmitted immediately through the LBR portal. A positive certificate of non-opposition is valid for 30 days and must be attached to the notarial deed of incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Only a regulated domiciliation agent may supply the statutory registered seat in Luxembourg; a pure virtual office alone will not satisfy the physical substance test for a manufacturing and retail entity. The cosplay costume and prop manufacturing activity requires a verifiable operational nexus, either a production facility in Luxembourg or a controlled EU subcontractor and fulfillment chain with documented commercial substance, physical storage, and customer-support presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk: approximate annual probability of 5-8% of an unannounced RCS or direct tax administration (ACD) substance inspection for this standard low-risk manufacturing-retail profile; foreign-ownership increases administrative-review probability to approximately 10% within the first year of operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 180-1 to 195 (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002; Law of 13 July 2016; Law of 2 September 2011 on business establishment
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with compulsory prior involvement of a Luxembourg notary
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized acte constitutif / articles of association filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for a SARL is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up before signature of the deed. Funds must be credited to a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) at a Luxembourg credit institution; the bank's certificate is attached to the notarial deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
Pro-forma resolution of the sole incorporator and first manager:
1. The incorporator subscribes the issued share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 100 equal parts of EUR 120 each, fully paid up into the Company’s blocked bank account as certified by [Bank].
2. The registered office is established at [Address], Luxembourg, and the manager is authorized to execute the lease and register the address.
3. [Name] is appointed sole manager with sole signatory power and full powers of administration and representation.
4. The manager is authorized to complete RCS registration, publish the RESA notice, obtain VAT and CCSS registration and apply for the business-establishment permit.
5. These resolutions take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability check and corporate name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) / lbr.lu online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS database for the proposed company name; submit a name-reservation request to avoid conflicts with existing trade names and trademarks and to confirm that the name contains valid corporate suffix 'SARL'.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, file an alternative name with a new availability certificate; appeal RCS refusal within 15 days to the tribunal of commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital account and capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) selected by the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Preregister the future company and open a temporary blocked account (compte bloqué) in the company's name; deposit the full minimum capital EUR 12,000. Obtain a bank attestation of deposit/blocking to deliver to the notary.
required_dossiers: Shareholder passport and proof of residence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries source of funds, provide bank statements and explanation; if the certificate is inaccurate, request a revised attestation and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary verifies shareholder identity, the bank capital certificate and the registered office agreement; drafts the final statutes; and convenes the incorporators for signature. The notary authenticates the deed and will file it with the RCS.
required_dossiers: Passport copies and proof of address
Consent of the first manager to appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests corrections, prepare an amended signature page or side letter; if the capital certificate is stale, obtain a new bank certificate before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS electronic registration and trade register extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the notarial deed, management consent and registered office evidence to the RCS via eRegistration. The RCS examines the legal validity, assigns a registration number and delivers the RCS extract (Extrait RCS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, the notary electronically files an additional brief or amending deed; correct within 15-day deadline and refile for no additional RCS fee except late fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA publication, VAT and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA; Centre commun de la sécurité sociale
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the notary arranges publication of the company's incorporation notice in RESA. Submit online VAT registration to the AEDT and employer registration to the CCSS, indicating commencement date of the costume manufacturing activity.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or registered office certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT application is returned, supply missing proof of address and RCS extract; for CCSS, correct social security declaration online and resubmit within statutory 8-day window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit and environmental/land-use clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy (General Directorate for SMEs) and the Administration de l'environnement; local commune
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the 'autorisation d'établissement' under the Law of 2 September 2011. If the workshop produces waste heat, waste water/discharges or airborne emissions, file a Class 4 environmental registration with the commune and environmental authority, and obtain pre-use inspections.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, supply missing technical plans, request ministerial reconsideration, or appeal to the administrative court within 3 months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des PME / Bureau des autorisations d'établissement
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to the craft trades, commercial activities and public service

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA report; Class 4 classified establishment registration (déclaration) under the Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with municipal wastewater standards (pH 6.5-9.5, suspended solids ≤35 mg/L, COD ≤125 mg/L); VOC emissions from synthetic wig/textile coating operations remain below 150 t/yr threshold but any solvent use must be declared; waste disposal under Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management and POPs/WEEE rules if applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours, structural load check by an approved engineering office, and occupational health/safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines before production hours.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Inland Revenue for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties. Central e-government portal: MyGuichet.lu; electronic filing gateways: eCDF for direct taxes and eTVA for VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of a Luxembourg SARL, the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) automatically issues the 11-digit national identification number (numéro d'identification) which serves as the direct-tax TIN. A separate VAT identification number (format: LU + 8 digits) must be applied for with the AEDT via the eTVA/MyGuichet portal after the entity has its registered office and effective activity address in Luxembourg. For foreign non-resident entities supplying taxable goods or services in Luxembourg, VAT registration must be filed directly with the AEDT; non-EU entities without a fixed establishment in Luxembourg are generally required to appoint a local VAT fiscal representative (représentant responsable) unless exempted under a mutual assistance convention. The SARL may commence export operations pending VAT issuance by using its national identification number, but invoicing with zero-rated VAT requires the active LU VAT number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Luxembourg SARL is a full resident corporate taxpayer subject to unlimited worldwide taxation: corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and annual net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune). It is not eligible for pass-through treatment; check-the-box classification is not recognized under Luxembourg law. The entity is not within a special tax-exempt zone, and the standard territorial scope is residence-based worldwide taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box regime. Available elections relevant to this SARL: (i) fiscal unity / group taxation (intégration fiscale) for corporate income tax, available only to 95%-owned Luxembourg resident subsidiaries of a Luxembourg resident parent; (ii) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT law, allowing the SARL to be treated as a single taxable person with affiliated Luxembourg entities; (iii) EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) election for taxable B2C distance sales of goods and cross-border B2C services, and Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) election for imports of consignments not exceeding EUR 150; (iv) no hybrid-mismatch election – mandatory anti-hybrid rules apply in accordance with ATAD as transposed by the Luxembourg law of 21 December 2018, with no elective opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover exemption threshold for small businesses (régime de la franchise); EUR 10,000 pan-EU threshold for intra-Community distance sales of goods and cross-border B2C telecommunications, broadcasting and electronic services; EUR 150 per-consignment threshold for IOSS import scheme. Outside these derogations, a taxable person is obliged to register for VAT from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg; there is no general turnover threshold above which the obligation crystallizes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or telemetric transaction reporting is currently in force in Luxembourg. B2B e-invoicing is voluntary and operates on PEPPOL-compatible standards. Mandatory electronic filing of VAT returns applies via the eTVA application on MyGuichet.lu, with monthly, quarterly or annual cycles depending on turnover; taxpayers subject to e-filing must also retain and produce on demand the Luxembourg SAF-T (fichier d'audit informatique) VAT audit file. All invoices must contain the statutory details required by Article 18 of the Luxembourg VAT law, including the LU VAT number, customer VAT number (for intra-Community supply), invoice date, description and VAT rate; e-invoice data must be retained for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated (0% VAT) treatment applies for: (i) direct export of goods physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the European Union, provided the goods leave the EU customs territory within 90 days of the supply; (ii) intra-Community supplies (B2B dispatches) to a customer holding a valid EU VAT identification number confirmed in VIES; (iii) export transport services and ancillary loading, handling and insurance services directly linked to the export movement; (iv) supplies of goods to approved customs warehousing or free-zone regimes where applicable. The manufacturer must obtain and archive evidence of physical exit, including customs export declaration numbers, transport documents and any third-party warehouse certificates; failure to substantiate the export within the statutory time limits disqualifies the zero rate and triggers reverse assessment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading (or CMR / Air Waybill)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Both the AEDT and Luxembourg Customs perform post-clearance audits (PCA) and cross-check the customs export declarations against the exporter's commercial and banking records; the Inward Remittance Certificate is examined to confirm that foreign currency proceeds are repatriated, normally within 180 days, in line with Luxembourg's balance-of-payments reporting expectations. Where zero-rating is claimed without valid export proof or is found to be fraudulent, the tax authority retrospectively reassesses VAT at the standard rate of 17% on the full invoice value, applies late-payment interest at 0.6% per month or part thereof, and imposes administrative fines which may reach EUR 12,500 or twice the evaded tax; criminal proceedings for serious VAT fraud may result in imprisonment of up to 5 years and additional monetary penalties. The standard five-year VAT assessment limitation period is extended to ten years where fraud is established, and the clawback may also trigger joint and several liability of the exporter's directors.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — the central monetary authority of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; prudential supervision over banks is exercised jointly by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and, for significant institutions, by the European Central Bank (ECB).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). Luxembourg law imposes no exchange-control restrictions on either current or capital account transactions, and no prior administrative authorization is required for the conversion, transfer, or repatriation of funds. Profit remittance from a Luxembourg SARL in the form of dividends is freely permitted subject to (i) verification of distributable reserves under Luxembourg corporate law (Law of 10 August 1915, Article 710-1), (ii) a 15% statutory dividend withholding tax reduced to 0% where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU applies (10% participation, 12-month holding) or where a double-tax treaty grants a reduced rate, and (iii) general anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening by the paying bank. There is no separate hurdle for unrestricted current-account convertibility or for reinvestment of export proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg and EU law impose no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion requirement for export receipts. A Luxembourg exporter may lawfully retain export proceeds in any currency, hold them in non-euro bank accounts, or convert them freely. In practice, banks must report to the BCL every cross-border payment exceeding EUR 12,500 for balance-of-payments statistics, and exporters must maintain underlying commercial documentation (invoice, customs declaration, bill of lading) to evidence the trade nature of the transaction. No conversion ratio, repatriation deadline, or compulsory US-dollar sale rule exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for ancillary payment collection and low-value supplier payouts; Low for treasury concentration and statutory capital holding. EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer, and Pockit can be onboarded for daily e-commerce collection from Shopify Payments/Stripe and for cross-border supplier payments under the PSD2 framework. Legal constraints: the EMI must hold a valid e-money license in an EU/EEA state and must passport into Luxembourg under PSD2; UK-only EMIs no longer enjoy passporting rights after Brexit; EMIs cannot hold a SARL's registered capital in escrow because they are not credit institutions and do not provide banking guarantees; funds held at an EMI are pooled and are not protected by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme (Fonds de Garantie Dépositaire Luxembourg). The prudent treasury policy is to cap EMI balances below EUR 50,000 and to settle daily via SWIFT/SEPA to a fully licensed Luxembourg bank. CSSF authorization may also be required if the EMI establishes a physical branch or outsources critical functions to Luxembourg.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one authorised director is not a fixed statutory condition, but is the universal de facto expectation of Luxembourg tier-1 banks during initial onboarding. Under the Luxembourg AML Law of 18 December 2015 and CSSF Circular 19/720, remote onboarding may be accepted through a video interview performed by a bank compliance officer, supplemented by digital signature and presentation of valid passport or national ID; however, for a non-resident-owned SARL, most banks require a physical kick-off meeting in Luxembourg or, alternatively, a notarised and apostilled identification package executed before the Luxembourg embassy or consulate in the UBO's jurisdiction. Source-of-wealth interviews are mandatory for all UBOs holding more than 25% of the share capital. A Luxembourg-registered independent trust or company service provider can facilitate the process, but cannot fully replace the UBO's identification and personal interview unless a explicit, notarised power of attorney is granted and the underlying identity data is fully documented.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO chain with intermediate holding entities in multiple jurisdictions creating an inability to identify natural persons with control or economic ownership of the SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete corporate structure chart; certificates of incorporation for every intermediate entity; statutory registers of members/shareholders; notarised passports and proof of residential address for all natural-person UBOs; a sworn source-of-funds declaration for the subscribed capital; audited financial statements of the parent entity; and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for each intermediate holding layer, including substance evidence such as staffing, premises, and tax filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived mismatch between the registered business purpose (licensed theatrical costume and cosplay apparel tailoring) and the projected high-volume e-commerce payment stream through Shopify Payments and Stripe, triggering elevated trade-based money-laundering risk scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a detailed business plan and product catalogue; contracted supplier invoices and purchase orders; platform account dashboards and settlement reports from Shopify and Stripe; customs declarations and bills of lading for export shipments; lease agreements and photos of the production facility; payroll and VAT returns; and an ISIC 3240 / NAICS 315280 classification confirmation letter issued by the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions-list, or politically-exposed-person (PEP) hits on one of the UBOs or on a counterparty in the supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver independent adverse-media and sanctions screening reports from reputable third-party databases (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv, LexisNexis) dated within 30 days; a detailed explanation letter from the affected person; official national and EU sanctions list search results; bank references or six-month bank statements of the affected party; and formal no-sanctions and good-standing certificates for the corporate counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High perceived geographic risk where the SARL sources materials from non-EEA countries (e.g., China, Hong Kong, Vietnam) and routes large trade payments to those jurisdictions, creating exposure to trade-based money laundering and customs fraud red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble a complete trade-file for every high-risk payment lane, containing signed pro-forma invoices; market-value documentary evidence; packing lists; original bills of lading or CMR documents; the beneficiary's bank and BIC/LEI confirmation; customs entry declarations; a supply-chain contract evidencing genuine trade; end-user certificates and anti-corruption warranties; and an independent transfer-pricing study if the supplier is a related party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance in Luxembourg for the SARL — especially where the entity is owned by non-residents and has minimal staff or physical footprint, prompting banks to question the entity's existence and beneficial-owner location.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a signed lease agreement on Luxembourg business premises; the RCS commercial register extract and publication certificate; employment contracts and Luxembourg social-security registrations for local staff; payroll summaries and withholding tax returns; quarterly VAT returns; six months of Luxembourg operating-account bank statements; corporate board-meeting minutes held in Luxembourg; and a corporate substance form confirming eligibility under Luxembourg substance-based anti-abuse rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For an equity capital injection from a foreign parent or shareholder, execute a SWIFT MT103 wire transfer from the shareholder's bank to the SARL's dedicated euro account at a Luxembourg credit institution. The payment must include a clear remittance reference (Field 70) quoting the board resolution approving the capital increase, the shareholder's name, and the purpose of the transfer. Standard SWIFT/ISO 20022 purpose codes accepted by Luxembourg banks for cross-border equity contributions include 'EQUI' (equity participation) or 'COVE' (capital/covering payments); for a shareholder loan, use 'LOAN' (lending) or 'ISOC' (intercompany intra-group financing). Verification requirements under Luxembourg AML and BCL balance-of-payments reporting rules include a certified board resolution; an updated share register and notarial deed for the capital increase; identification and source-of-funds documentation for the contributing shareholder; a signed subscription agreement; and confirmation that the receiving bank has been provided with an LEI and the RCS registration number. All amounts exceeding EUR 12,500 are automatically captured in the bank's monthly BOP reporting to the BCL, and no prior exchange-control permission is required from the BCL or the Ministry of Finance. For non-EU-source funds, the originating bank must apply standard sanctions screening and may require the shareholder's bank to confirm the beneficial owner before crediting the account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for cosplay prop and apparel raw materials and manufacturing services should be settled through standard institutional clearing rails. Direct supplier payments in EUR, USD, or CNY are sent via SWIFT MT103 from the Luxembourg operational account to the beneficiary bank's BIC, with proper invoice and contract references in Field 70 and a valid ISO 20022 purpose code such as 'PURT' (purchase of goods) or 'SUPP' (supplier payment). For large or strategic orders, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) governed by the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600) provides secure deferred payment against presentation of transport documents, commercial invoice, packing list, inspection certificate, and beneficiary-drawn draft. Alternatively, Documentary Collection under URC 522 may be used for lower-cost, lower-risk trades. Where the counterparty is in the EU, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) can be used for euro-denominated disbursements, while non-euro payments must use SWIFT. For the buyer-side payment, the Luxembourg bank will screen the beneficiary against sanctions lists and may request the beneficiary's LEI or BIC plus copies of the customs export declarations to corroborate the declared commercial purpose. Proceeds from Shopify Payments and Stripe are collected in the merchant's e-money or card-acquiring settlement bank, then swept via SWIFT/SEPA to the Luxembourg SARL's concentration account, preserving a clean audit trail and enabling daily liquidity consolidation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forward contracts with a Luxembourg or EU credit institution, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or a long-form FX confirmation, limited to hedges of projected USD receivables from Shopify/Stripe sales.
Offshore EUR/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) settled in USD, executed with an EU credit institution licensed to provide CNH hedging and subject to the bank's internal China-risk limits.
EUR/USD cross-currency swaps exchanged at both maturity and principal expiry, permissible for hedging the currency risk of a long-term multi-year licensing or distribution contract.

Plain vanilla EUR/USD FX options (purchased and written) with a premium budget, permissible for asymmetric hedging where the SARL seeks downside protection without forfeiting upside conversion benefits.

Rolling physical FX swaps (FX swap/collateral swap) between the entity's EUR cash pool and USD or CNH operatonal currencies, executed with the primary relationship bank under an FCA-authorised or CSSF-supervised dealing desk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (approved financial statements) filing and publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval within six months of financial year-end; filing within one month after approval. For a calendar-year SARL, approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a fine of EUR 750 to EUR 25,000 per fiscal year (Company Law Art. 1676). If annual accounts remain unfiled for two consecutive fiscal years, the RCS may, after notice, strike the company off or initiate compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and net wealth tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing by 30 June following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; extensions available upon written request. Non-calendar year-ends align with the statutory tax return timetable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to 10% of the assessed tax plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.6% on unpaid tax; persistent failure may lead to coercive collection and criminal tax-fraud proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Updates must be filed within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership or UBO information. No annual no-change statement is mandated, but the RBE data must be kept accurate and verified at each ordinary general meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update UBO information is punishable by criminal fines and imprisonment under the Law of 13 January 2019; continued non-compliance may be referred to the Public Prosecutor's Office. No direct strike-off solely for UBO default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and corporate records/register audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records maintained at the registered office; no registration with an external authority unless accompanied by an amendment filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ordinary general meeting must be convened at least once per calendar year and within six months of the financial year-end; minutes and register entries must be completed without delay after the meeting and kept indefinitely.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM and maintain statutory registers may render managers jointly and severally liable for resulting damages; a shareholder may seek court-ordered dissolution or an injunctive remedy.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is triggered for a SARL exceeding two of the following three thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce 50 employees; audit is also required if the articles of association so provide or if the entity is part of a consolidated group under Luxembourg legal requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2008 (accounting and annual accounts), itself aligned with EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is permitted for annual accounts of SARLs where law allows and is used for consolidation by listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg law requires continuous accuracy of the RBE rather than a fixed annual re-filing. Following any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership, the SARL must update its internal shareholders register and file the UBO modification with the RBE within 30 days. At the AGM, management must review the UBO data and confirm that no uncorrected outdated information remains; if no change occurred, no RBE filing is due for that year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $2,800 - $7,500 per year for Luxembourg registered office and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,500 - $12,000 per year for an independent Réviseur d'Entreprises Agréé, depending on activity volume and filings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% statutory corporate income tax (impot sur le revenu des collectivites); combined headline burden in Luxembourg City for tax year 2024: 17% CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax (impot commercial communal) + 7% employment fund solidarity surcharge on CIT = approximately 24.94% aggregate effective burden for a resident SARL.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% net income exemption under the Luxembourg IP box regime for qualifying licensed theatrical designs and costume/apparel intellectual property; 100%/99% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (minimum 10% holding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost, 12-month holding condition where applicable); investment tax credit of 6% to 13% for new qualifying tangible and intangible fixed assets; R&D tax credit of 20% on qualifying R&D expenses up to EUR 750,000 per tax year; effective rate on qualifying IP box income can be reduced to approximately 4.94% to 5.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited - no statutory expiry (indefinite carryforward of Luxembourg tax losses; carryback is not permitted; separate tracking required for IP box losses post-2021 reform)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 800 - Declaration pour l'impot sur le revenu des collectivites, l'impot commercial communal et l'impot sur la fortune; mandatory electronic filing through the eCDF (electronic Corporate Declaration Framework) portal on MyGuichet.lu using Luxtrust authentication.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory filing deadline is 30 June of the year following the tax year-end; where the annual accounts have not been approved by the general meeting before that date, the deadline may be extended to 30 November provided the eCDF extension is registered; the Luxembourg tax administration may issue an individual filing notice with a specific deadline of at least 30 days.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, legal form (SARL), registered office address, Luxembourg RCS number (Registre de Commerce et des Societes), business registration number, and tax file number (numero de dossier fiscal).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Luxembourg SARL is a resident taxpayer; full identification is mandatory even when 100% of share capital is held by non-residents; where the SARL acts as a permanent establishment of a foreign enterprise, identify the PE address and the local fiscal representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates; for a standard calendar-year SARL, enter 01.01.YYYY to 31.12.YYYY.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SARL closes accounts on a non-calendar date, the tax period must align with the statutory accounts; no special non-resident treatment applies to a resident SARL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total aggregate assets per the statutory balance sheet prepared under Luxembourg GAAP or IFRS as adopted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No deviation for non-resident shareholders; the balance sheet total also serves as the base for net wealth tax filing thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit (resultat courant avant impot) as derived from the statutory profit and loss account before corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjustments for permanent establishment allocation do not apply to the resident SARL; intra-group cosplay manufacturing invoices must be booked at arm's length values.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable basis (benefice imposable) determined after reclassification, transfer pricing corrections, non-deductible expenses, and deduction of available tax losses carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter all Luxembourg-source and worldwide income of the resident SARL; foreign business profits covered by a tax treaty are exempt or credited only if properly documented in the annexes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 80% exemption on net qualifying income derived from qualifying intellectual property (licensed theatrical costume designs, synthetic wig manufacturing processes, cosplay apparel brand trademarks).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IP box relief attaches at entity level; non-resident shareholders cannot claim it by treaty; annex the IP asset register and tracking of qualifying expenditure and income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the credit d'impot pour investissement at 6% or 8% for new qualifying fixed assets (13%/14% for qualifying environmental or digital assets in specified regions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit is granted to the resident SARL only and reduces aggregate CIT/ICC; a non-resident shareholder has no direct entitlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable basis for the communal trade tax after allocation factors, including the minimum dormant basis of EUR 9,750 where no positive basis arises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: ICC is levied on the resident SARL using Luxembourg City's 6.75% rate in the default scenario; verify municipal tariff of the registered office address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax unit value (valeur unitaire) computed on net asset value as at 1 January of the assessment year; standard rate 0.5%, reduced to 0.05% for net wealth below EUR 500,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A resident SARL reports worldwide net assets subject to treaty and participation-exemption carve-outs; non-resident shareholders are not subject to Luxembourg net wealth tax on the SARL's assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separate line for exempt dividends and capital gains from qualified holdings (minimum 10% or EUR 1.2 million cost, 12-month holding), supported by an annex stating the subsidiary jurisdiction, holding period, and accounting method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This exemption applies to the SARL itself as beneficiary; the non-resident parent must obtain its own treaty relief or Parent-Subsidiary Directive clearance on distribution out of Luxembourg.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 0.5% on the assessed tax, capped at 25% of the tax due; late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month; formal non-filing after demand is subject to administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 under Section 168 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law; willful misdeclaration escalates to criminal tax fraud with imprisonment up to 2 years (5 years aggravated) and fines up to EUR 250,000, plus publication of the conviction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory withholding tax on all dividend distributions made by a Luxembourg SARL to shareholders, whether resident or non-resident, unless a specific statutory, treaty, or EU Directive exemption applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced or zero dividend withholding rate, the beneficial-owner shareholder must deliver to the paying SARL before the distribution: (i) a valid tax residence certificate (certificat de residence) issued by the shareholder's competent tax authority, (ii) an ownership certificate evidencing the shareholding percentage and holding period, and (iii) a Form 850/812 treaty relief application where required; the Luxembourg payer applies the reduced rate at source where the documentation is complete; if 15% was withheld, the shareholder may file a refund claim with the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) within the applicable statutory limitation period (generally until the end of the fifth year following the distribution), supported by an apostilled TRC and ownership statement; the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive grants 0% withholding where the parent holds at least 10% of the SARL for a 12-month period, and Luxembourg's participation exemption may also support a 0% liquidation-distribution outcome; substance of the SARL and the parent must be genuine to withstand GAAR/abuse-of-law review.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg generally imposes no withholding tax on outbound interest and royalty payments (0% statutory rate); this applies to cosplay brand-license royalties, costume design licensing fees, and intercompany debt interest paid by the SARL to non-residents; exceptions exist for certain profit-participating instruments and where payments are recharacterized as constructive dividends by substance-abuse or transfer-pricing audit; under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, a 0% rate is available on payments to EU associated companies (25% direct holding, 24-month ownership condition) without further Luxembourg withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 - Luxembourg entity or Luxembourg group net turnover threshold above which a contemporaneous Local File and Master File must be maintained and produced on request; EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue triggers mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting; TP documentation must also be prepared whenever the SARL engages in cross-border intercompany transactions with cosplay costume manufacturing affiliates, brand-IP licensees, or foreign distribution entities, regardless of turnover, where the tax administration demands documentation.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) for licensing and commodity apparel sales
Resale Price Method for distribution of cosplay costumes by related distributors
Cost Plus Method for manufacturing of theatrical prop apparel and synthetic wigs
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) as the most common practical method for the SARL's manufacturing and retail functions
Profit Split Method for integrated multi-party IP exploitation arrangements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations law comparable to zero-tax jurisdictions; however, genuine substance is mandatory for treaty and EU Directive benefits under the abuse-of-law doctrine (Section 6 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law, Abgabenordnung), the EU ATAD GAAR, and the OECD principal-purpose test; indicators of substantive operation for the cosplay SARL include local premises, employees with real decision-making authority, local board meetings, operational bank accounts (Stripe/Shopify settlement accounts in Luxembourg), and a physical supply chain for costume and wig manufacturing; a shell-type SARL with foreign resident directors, no staff, no premises, and only passive IP-holding functions will be recharacterized, denied treaty benefits, and reassessed with penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Deliberate Underreporting of E-commerce Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission or misstatement of Stripe and Shopify Payments turnover generated from online cosplay prop and apparel sales; off-book cash or crypto settlements, fictitious supplier invoices, and engineered inventory shrinkage used to reduce profit before tax in the Form 800 filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction for tax fraud under Sections 396-397 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law: fine of up to EUR 250,000 (aggravated cases) and imprisonment of up to 2 years (up to 5 years in aggravated or organized cases); mandatory full restitution of evaded corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; administrative penalties up to 25% of the additional assessment; publication of the judgment in official records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause the submission of a false Form 800 are jointly and severally liable for the SARL's civil restitution and tax debts; personal responsibility extends through the action en comblement du passif where gross fault contributed to insolvency; criminal courts may impose travel bans, seizure of personal assets, immediate imprisonment, and disqualification from serving as directors of any Luxembourg company for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Abuse of Law (Sham Cosplay IP Structure)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishment of the SARL as a zero-substance shell with no premises, no employees, and no real manufacturing activity, used solely to hold licensed theatrical costume and wig IP, collect royalties from foreign licensees, and distribute tax-privileged dividends to non-residents; artificial interposition in the IP chain with no commercial rationality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization and disregard of the arrangement by the ACD pursuant to Section 6 of the General Tax Law; denial of treaty and Parent-Subsidiary Directive benefits; retroactive 15% dividend withholding tax assessment; disallowance of IP box deductions; transfer-pricing adjustments under Article 56bis LIR; additional tax penalties of up to 25% plus monthly interest; criminal penalties in cases of intentional fraud as noted above.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors implicated in the sham arrangement face joint and several liability for the additional assessments, civil restitution to the Luxembourg State, personal fines, travel restrictions, and imprisonment where the court finds complicity in tax fraud; Luxembourg courts pierce the corporate veil for fraudulent misuse of the SARL legal form.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Non-Compliance and Money-Laundering Integration Risks
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematic acceptance of high-volume Stripe/Shopify payments with no know-your-customer controls, no transaction monitoring, unresolved beneficial-ownership ambiguity, or movement of e-commerce proceeds through blocking accounts in a manner designed to disguise the origin of criminal property.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended): CSSF administrative fines, disciplinary sanctions, and criminal penalties for money laundering of up to EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years; freezing orders and forfeiture of proceeds; the SARL's business license and payment-rail agreements (Stripe/Shopify) may be terminated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly or negligently facilitate laundering through the cosplay retail enterprise are criminally indictable in their personal capacity; asset forfeiture orders, international travel bans via INTERPOL Red Notices, and custodial sentences apply; professional disqualification and personal restitution of laundered values are routinely ordered by Luxembourg criminal courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Bankruptcy and Over-Distribution of Capital
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing the SARL's business while insolvent; payment of dividends or shareholder loans when net assets have fallen below the subscribed share capital; false annual accounts overstating cosplay inventory value; preferential payments to foreign shareholders designed to frustrate Luxembourg creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Action en comblement du passif before the Luxembourg commercial court: directors are personally ordered to satisfy the entire shortfall where gross mismanagement (faute de gestion) caused the insolvency; criminal bankruptcy (banqueroute) sanctions include imprisonment of 1 month to 5 years, fines, and prohibition from conducting any commercial or managerial activity for up to 10 years; tax claims rank as privileged and are pursued through the bankruptcy liquidation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability of directors without limitation of liability where distributions are made contrary to the SARL rules of the Luxembourg Companies Law; the corporate veil is pierced and directors' personal assets are exposed; travel bans, judicial liquidation supervision, and imprisonment are available sanctions; personal liability attaches to each director who knowingly participated in the over-distribution resolution.
